pageCache.text:
Welcome Message from the Headteacher
Welcome to Southern Road Primary School.
Having worked at Southern Road for several years, I feel an immense sense of pride each and every day in our wonderfully diverse community of children, parents, and staff. It is through our strong collaboration that we ensure all children are supported to achieve their very best.
Academic achievement is a key focus at our school, and we encourage all pupils to uphold the Southern Road standards for behaviour and learning. Our children are taught to be resilient and strive for success in everything they do.
In our most recent Ofsted report, inspectors recognised that our children have the opportunity to “develop their talents and interests” through a wide range of sporting and musical activities, as well as enriching educational visits. Our pastoral care is exceptional; we are committed to keeping all children safe and well supported both in and out of school, and we work closely with families to overcome any barriers to learning.
As Headteacher, I am incredibly proud of our experienced and dedicated staff, who go above and beyond every day to help our children reach their full potential.
We warmly welcome visits to the school and look forward to working in partnership with you to create the best possible learning experiences for all children at Southern Road Primary School.
Ms Helen YearnshireHeadteacher, Southern Road Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: SMSC British Values – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development and British Values
At Southern Road we recognise that the personal development of pupils, spiritually, morally, socially and culturally, plays a significant part in their ability to learn and achieve. We therefore aim to provide an education that provides pupils with opportunities to explore and develop their own values and beliefs, spiritual awareness, high standards of personal behaviour, a positive caring attitude towards other people, an understanding of their social and cultural traditions and an appreciation of the diversity and richness of other cultures.
All curriculum areas have a contribution to make to the child’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural development and opportunities for this will be planned in each area of the curriculum.
Spiritual Development
Our children are encouraged to reflect on the predominant religious and moral values that underpin our democratic and multi-cultural British society. Through Religious Education lessons, Collective Worship, visiting places of worship and celebratory events, our children learn about the similarities and differences of other religions and are encouraged to reflect on their own beliefs whilst tolerating the different viewpoints of others including those who do not have a religious faith.
We aim to develop our children spiritually by supporting them to;
Throughout areas of the curriculum, children are presented with moral issues for debate, discussion and reflection. Such issues enable and encourage our children to discuss British values and understand how these are relevant to them.
The children are supported in their moral development through discussion, teaching and opportunities to:
Children have a wide range of opportunities to work collaboratively within class and across year groups. We promote ‘Buddy Systems’ for children new to the school and have appointed children as ‘Peer Mediators’ who actively support other children throughout break-time and lunchtimes.
Southern Road is at the heart of the local community and we encourage pupils to show care and consideration for others through charitable work and young citizenship. Opportunities are planned where possible to link the curriculum to charities within the community, such as raising funds for Richard House Children’s Hospice or donating food to Newham foodbank. The enabling enterprise lessons we provide allow children to develop skills such as teamwork and leadership as well as expanding their knowledge of businesses within the local area and wider community. The School Council ensure that all children can influence decision making in school through the democratic processes and regular pupil surveys that are conducted.
There is a strong emphasis throughout the Personal Health and Relationship areas of study on individual rights and responsibilities including respect and valuing difference in the way people choose to live in modern British Society.
Our children are encouraged to develop socially by:
Cultural Development
At Southern Road Primary School we value the diverse ethnic background of all pupils and families and undertake a variety of events to celebrate these, such as ‘Cultural Diversity Week,’ which takes place during the Autumn Term. We have found this approach to be enriching for all parties as it teaches tolerance and respect for the differences in our community and the wider world.
Through our English, Geography, History, French, Art, Music, Dance, RE and PSHE curriculum and wide programme of educational visits there are a wide range of learning opportunities which have strong links to the United Kingdom, through which we develop our children’s cultural understanding by enabling children to:
The Department for Education’s (2011) five-part definition of British values as found in the Prevent Strategy is:
Democracy forms an important part of life at Southern Road. Our Governing Body is elected, representative of the British democratic process. Candidates from the school staff, parents, community and Local Authority can stand for election and the Governing Body meet regularly to discuss key issues and help shape the community that is Southern Road Primary School. We have an active School Council, with representatives from each class elected at the beginning of the academic year. School Council meets regularly to discuss school issues and this year has a focus on making links between school and the community.
We are in a privileged position that our school building is used as a polling station for elections, giving us the opportunity to gain some understanding of how voting works.
As part of our curriculum, children learn about British and international History, and how some countries are run. We learn about rules in sport/games as part of our PE lessons and have visits from the police and fire brigade to learn about rules in our community.
We have an ethos and values which can be found in our prospectus and on and on our website, we also have a behaviour policy which includes a hierarchy of consequences and a rewards system. In addition to the policies and information displayed on our website we also have a newsletter which communicates events and learning to parents.
Southern Road ensures every individual achieves their best through high expectations for all, which focus on confidence, creativity and care. Through our teaching of PSHE/Citizenship and we develop an understanding human and children’s rights and responsibilities.
Our school policies incorporate individual liberty and can be found on the website, or hard copies are available on request from the school office.
We expect our learners to be respectful, confident and positive individuals. We encourage every child to care about, and have respect for, their learning, each other and our environment. By being socially and emotionally intelligent, understanding about themselves and each other, our children will make the right choices and experience positive relationships now and in the future.
Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs
Not only do we demonstrate tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs, we positively embrace them. We teach children the values of their own opinions as well as those of others. Examples of this include taking pupils out on educational visits to different places of worship, and following the Newham Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education that educates pupils about all of the main belief systems in the UK.
At Southern Road Primary School we believe that, through promoting British values, our children will become responsible citizens for the future who show mutual respect and tolerance of others, value their own liberty and understand the rules of law and democracy whilst demonstrating care and compassion for all.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap-Around Childcare – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Childcare at Southern Road Primary School
At Southern Road Primary School, we offer on-site Breakfast Club and After-School Smart Club provision to support busy working families while extending social, learning and play opportunities for our pupils.
Our dedicated and qualified supervision staff aim to ensure that children have the best possible experience while enjoying a range of age-appropriate activities and games in a safe and welcoming environment.
Southern Road Primary School also offers free Breakfast Club and After-School Smart Club places to eligible working parents when their child is in Reception.
The Benefits of Wraparound Childcare
Good-quality wraparound childcare can have a positive impact on children’s outcomes.
Research by NatCen has shown that participating in organised sports and attending after-school clubs can help improve primary school children’s academic performance and social skills.
Among disadvantaged children, those who attended after-school clubs performed better than peers who did not participate, achieving on average a two-point higher total score in their Key Stage 2 assessments in English, maths and science.
Research has also shown that children who participate in organised sports and physical activities during primary school can demonstrate better social, emotional and behavioural skills.
FREE BREAKFAST CLUB
Breakfast for All
At Southern Road Primary School, we believe that no child should start the school day too hungry to learn.
It is important for pupils to start their day with a nutritious breakfast. Evidence shows that providing a healthy breakfast at the beginning of the school day can contribute to improved readiness to learn, increased concentration, and improved wellbeing and behaviour.
Following our successful application to the Government’s Free Breakfast Club Programme, Southern Road Primary School is delighted to provide a FREE Breakfast Club for all pupils from Reception to Year 6.
FREE Breakfast Club
8:10am – 8:40am FREE for Reception to Year 6
The free provision is available every school day during term time, subject to availability.
Children attending will have the opportunity to enjoy breakfast in a welcoming and positive environment before beginning their school day, helping them arrive in class settled, prepared and ready to learn.
Breakfast Club Times & Charges
Breakfast Club operates during term time, Monday to Friday, excluding school INSET days and Bank Holidays.
7:30am – 8:10am
£5.00 per child, per session
This is our paid early Breakfast Club for families who require an earlier drop-off.
8:10am – 8:40am
This session is provided through the Government’s Free Breakfast Club Programme and is available to pupils from Reception to Year 6.
All Breakfast Club sessions must be booked in advance through the MCAS app.
Places are limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Booking Breakfast Club Through MCAS
Parents and carers must:
Register their child for Breakfast Club.
Book the required sessions through the MCAS app.
Book sessions in advance.
Ensure they have a confirmed booking before bringing their child to Breakfast Club.
Book early to avoid disappointment.
Please do not bring your child to Breakfast Club without a confirmed MCAS booking.
All bookings are subject to the Southern Road Primary School Before and After School Provision Terms and Conditions.
Breakfast and Activities
Children attending Breakfast Club will receive a healthy and nutritious breakfast alongside a range of suitable activities before going to their classrooms.
Our provision includes opportunities for mentally and physically stimulating activities to help children prepare for the school day.
Breakfast options aim to provide nutritious food that supports children’s concentration, attention and readiness to learn.
Changes to Our Previous Breakfast Provision
Previously, bagels were made available to children in classrooms as part of our morning breakfast provision.
As Southern Road Primary School has now joined the Government’s Free Breakfast Club Programme, the previous classroom bagel provision will no longer operate.
Families wishing to access the free breakfast provision should instead book their child into the:
8:10am – 8:40am FREE Breakfast Club through MCAS.
We are delighted to offer this provision to our families and hope it provides additional support to parents and carers while ensuring children have the opportunity to begin their day with breakfast and arrive in class ready to learn.
AFTER-SCHOOL SMART CLUB
Our After-School Smart Club provides children with a safe, enjoyable and stimulating environment at the end of the school day.
Smart Club operates during term time, Monday to Friday, excluding school INSET days and Bank Holidays.
Smart Club Times & Charges
3:00pm – 5:15pm: £8.00 per child, per session
3:00pm – 5:45pm: £10.00 per child, per session
Without Prior Booking
Where a child attends without a prior booking, the following charges apply:
3:15pm – 5:15pm: £9.00
3:15pm – 5:45pm: £11.00
Sibling discounts may apply.
Eligible working parents may receive free Smart Club provision while their child is in Reception.
What Happens at Smart Club?
Our SMART Club is designed to provide a positive and enjoyable conclusion to the school day.
Sessions vary and can include:
Indoor and outdoor activities
Games and creative activities
Opportunities to socialise with other children
Children are encouraged to participate in physical activities wherever appropriate. Activities are inclusive and designed to keep children active through play while supporting the development of social skills, self-esteem, balance, coordination and wellbeing.
Children attending Smart Club are also provided with a suitable snack.
Late Collection Charges
Parents and carers must ensure that children are collected within their booked session.
Where a child has not been booked into Smart Club and remains at school after the normal collection time, the applicable full Smart Club charge will be applied.
Collection up to 5:15pm: £9.00
Collection up to 5:45pm: £11.00
Parents should therefore ensure that the correct Smart Club session is booked in advance through MCAS.
Cancellations, Changes and Absence
Please ensure that you only book sessions your child requires.
We are unable to offer refunds where parents need to change booked days at short notice or where a child is absent on the day of their booked session.
This is because staffing is arranged in advance in accordance with health and safety requirements and required staff-to-child ratios.
Please refer to our Wraparound Childcare Terms and Conditions for full details regarding bookings, cancellations and charges.
Register for Wraparound Childcare
Before using our Breakfast Club or After-School Smart Club, parents and carers must register their child for our wraparound childcare provision.
Wraparound Childcare Registration Form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdQR3BTcvEt6JZw5QJVX3qd6GT0tLgC-Nrj23WXoFVSkuseUg/viewform
Once registered, parents should use the MCAS app to make the required bookings.
Parent Booking Guide

pageCache.pageTitle: Expansion of 30 hours childcare – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Expansion of 30 hours childcare
Starting from April 2024, existing child-care support will be expanded in phases. Eligibility criteria applies.
• From April 2024, working parents of 2- year-olds will be able to access 15 hours childcare support.
By September 2025, working parents with children aged 9 months old to when they start school will be eligible for 30 hours childcare support.
Am I eligible? Your child will qualify for a free place if both parents in a two parent family are working (or in a sole parent family, the lone parent must be working) and each parent on average earns:
• a weekly minimum equivalent to 16 hours at National Minimum Wage (NMW) or National Living Wage (NLW) • less than £100,000 per year.
If you cannot work you may still be eligible if your partner works and you access a qualifying disability or carers benefit. How can I apply? If you think you are eligible, you will be able to apply for your place via childcarechoices.gov.uk
You will be given an eligibility code if successful. Email this to admission@southernroadprimary.com. You will have to reconfirm eligibility every 3 months.
When is my child entitled to a free place? You must apply a term ahead to get access to the free hours from the term after i.e. apply now for a place next term
If your child’s 2nd birthday is between the following we recommend you apply in this period:
Your child will become entitled to their free place from:
1 January – 31 March
the start of the summer term (from April 2024)
the start of the autumn term (from September 2024)
1 September – 31 December
the start of the spring term (from January 2025)

pageCache.pageTitle: Schools Counselling Partnership – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Ms Jaime North MBACP
Here at Southern Road we believe wellbeing and mental health play a pivotal role in the development of our students and our school community.
By having an in-house counsellor we are able to offer a range of wellbeing interventions to support our students, parents and staff. Our dedicated school counsellor, Jaime, is on hand to assist you and your child with any worries or challenges they may be experiencing. We work closely to ensure your child receives the support they need to work through any difficulties or emotional distress.
Jaime provides individual 1:1 therapy sessions. Each session is tailored to meet the needs of the child by offering talking therapy with a creative approach to ensure a safe space where feelings and emotions can be shared and processed without judgment or expectations.
School/Parent Partnerships
As parents you will be invited to meet Jaime and to share your experiences of your child and help to build a picture of what their presenting issues may be, this could be anything from challenging friendships groups and finding it hard to fit in, to supporting your child with the loss of a loved one or a parental separation. As well as helping with anxiety and stress due to their environment or life circumstances.
In addition to supporting the children Jaime also provides support and guidance for our parents. This can look like 1:1 counselling sessions, regular check ins or working with parent and child together to build upon the relationship.
We understand that today’s climate can be challenging and tough for parents, navigating life and the impact of the cost of living crisis as well as things like our own personal health needs and the demands of every day life, things can become overwhelming.
By sharing some of these life challenges it can help make things more manageable and help parents to understand themselves better and be more emotionally available for their children.
We understand that for many parents they have to work during school times so we take pride in offering a flexible service where parents can access support at a time to fit around their work/home life balance.
Several of our staff members have also benefited from engaging in wellbeing support. We believe that as a whole school community it is essential we support the wellbeing of our staff so they are able to support the children in our care.
Jaime has over 30 years of experience working in a school and community environment so has first hand knowledge of the challenges faced.
Please if you feel any of the services listed above would benefit you or your child please do not hesitate to reach out for an initial consultation.
All individual cases will be treated with the upmost respect and confidentiality is key to the work we do.
Jaime can be contacted via email or telephone
Jnorth19.316@southernroadprimary.com
Counsellingwithjaime@gmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents Communication App – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
MyChildAtSchool (MCAS)
MyChildAtSchool (MCAS) is our online parent portal and mobile app, designed to make it easier for families to stay connected with the school and manage important school-related activities in one convenient place.
MCAS provides parents and carers with secure access to information relating to their child and helps improve communication between home and school. By bringing key services together in one system, MCAS enables families to access information and complete important tasks quickly and conveniently.
At our school, MCAS is used for:
How MCAS supports families
MCAS gives parents and carers one secure and convenient place to interact with the school. The mobile app means important information and services can be accessed from a smartphone or tablet, helping families manage bookings, appointments and school information more easily.
How MCAS supports the school
Using MCAS helps the school communicate with families efficiently and reduces the need for separate paper forms and systems. Information submitted by parents can be managed securely within our school management system, helping us maintain accurate and up-to-date records.
We encourage all parents and carers to regularly check the MCAS app to ensure they do not miss important school communications, booking information or requests to update their child’s details.
Getting Started with MCAS (Bromcom)
Registering is quick and easy. In the coming days, you will receive an email and/or text with details on how to set up your My Child at School account. Please follow the instructions provided in the message.
Parents Guide:Getting set up on Bromcom(MCAS)
Be assured that Bromcom is fully compliant with data protection regulations. Your personal information will remain secure and will not be shared with any third parties.
Why download the MCAS App?
If you have an Android or Apple smartphone, we strongly encourage you to download the My Child at School app. Here’s why:
No need to log in each time to check messages or attachments.
All school messages are stored in one place for easy access.
You’ll receive instant alerts directly to your phone.
You help us cut down on paper and reduce admin costs.
You can download the MCAS app for free from the App Store or Google Play Store.
Thank you for your continued support as we make this exciting move to Bromcom!

pageCache.pageTitle: Medical information – Southern Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Why It’s Important for Parents to Share Medical Information With the School
At our school, the health, safety, and wellbeing of every student is our top priority. To support this, it is essential that parents and carers inform us of any medical conditions, diagnoses, or health concerns that may affect their child during the school day.
When the school is aware of a student’s medical needs, we can:
Provide appropriate care and support, including administering medication when required.
Plan for emergencies and ensure staff know how to respond quickly and safely.
Make necessary adjustments to classroom activities, physical education, outings, and school events.
Work collaboratively with families and healthcare professionals to support each child’s ongoing health needs.
Maintain a safe and inclusive environment, ensuring students with medical conditions are fully supported in their learning and wellbeing.
All medical information shared with the school is handled confidentially and used only for the purpose of keeping students safe and supported. It is stored securely and shared only with staff members who need this information to care for your child appropriately.
Keeping us updated—especially if a condition changes or new information becomes available—helps ensure we can continue to meet the needs of every learner.
If you have any questions or need to update your child’s medical information, please contact the school office.
